correction.text: the shape unchanged, but for 1958 only (14 February to 2 August 1958); for 1959 Iraq is the Iraqi Republic and Jordan the Kingdom of Jordan (see the kingdom-of-jordan dossier's 1959 keyframe)

keyframe_review.note: 537,952 km2 against the infobox's 533,314 km2 (ratio 1.01): the outline of Iraq plus Jordan with the West Bank. The page gives the federation only 14 February to 2 August 1958, so the 1959 year of the Cliopatria shape is wrong; the rendering agent should draw the successors for 1959. The shape is Cliopatria's union of the two members, since the page gives no land of its own.

region.text: the territory of Iraq and Jordan, the two members

ledger.note: 14 February 1958: Iraq and Jordan form the Arab Federation. 'Officially formed on 14 February 1958, the Arab Union or Arab Federation united foreign policy and defense of each country'; formed in answer to the United Arab Republic ('In early 1958, Nasser ... convincing Syria and Egypt to unite'). Cliopatria's single shape covers both states; the page does not say what land each contributed.

region.text: Iraq, one of the two members

ledger.note: 14 February 1958: the Kingdom of Iraq joins (members: Iraq and Jordan). Nuri al-Said resigned as Iraqi Prime Minister to become Premier of the Arab Union; Baghdad is the federation's capital.

region.text: Jordan, the other member, East and West Bank

ledger.note: 14 February 1958: the Kingdom of Jordan joins; Jordan's own Prime Minister is Ibrahim Hashem.

region.text: Iraq, one of the two members

ledger.note: 14 July 1958: the Iraqi coup removes Iraq. 'Faisal II was deposed by a military coup on 14 July'; 'both the Hashemite regime fell and with it the short-lived Arab Federation'. Iraq passes to the republic (iraqi-republic dossier, founded the same day); the formal dissolution follows on 2 August.

region.text: Jordan, the other member, East and West Bank

ledger.note: 2 August 1958: Jordan resumes its separate existence. 'the new Iraqi government officially dissolved the Federation on 2 August 1958'; the page does not say what Jordan took back, only that the Federation ended.

2 August 1958: the Arab Federation is dissolved. 'The Hashemite Arab Federation was a short-lived confederation that lasted from 14 February to 2 August 1958.' Cliopatria extends the shape to 1959, which the keyframe review corrects.

certainty.note: The federation drew no frontier of its own; its outline is the two members' frontiers, which the page does not describe.

notes: Written by me-10-j from one page (the page budget is 1-2). CLIOPATRIA: one shape, 1958-1959, 537,952 km2; the federation lasted 14 February to 2 August 1958, so 1959 is wrong, and Cliopatria has no Iraq or Jordan shape for 1958-1959 (its Iraqi Republic starts in 1960). The kingdom-of-jordan dossier adds a 1959 keyframe; the iraqi-republic dossier (founded 14 July 1958, with arab-federation among its predecessors) should cover Iraq for 1959. ENDING: the Iraqi coup of 14 July 1958 removed the Iraqi monarchy and 'with it the short-lived Arab Federation'; the formal dissolution is 2 August; the dossier ends on the formal date. No war: 'During the summer of 1958, UAR troop movements to the Syrian border instigated the Arab Federation to mobilize troops' is the only military line on the page. The UAR formation date (1 February 1958 on its own dossier) is not on this page. NOT READ: the 14 July Revolution page and the union's constitution.
